metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially after recent spikes or high volatility; apply downward bias correction by 5–15% for periods with recent upward momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model tends to ignore mean reversion; force a slight downward adjustment toward recent 7–14 day moving average.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 48.25 → 50.19) are common; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 1.2x 30-day average to prevent overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., 48.03 → 46.67), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% for first 3–5 days post-spike.
- In low-sentiment environments, model exhibits persistent upward bias; use sentiment as proxy for volatility: if sentiment = 0, reduce forecast by 3–7% for 3–7 day horizon.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 49.61 → 35.94), model overreacts; apply “reversion buffer” — reduce forecast by 10–20% for 5–10 day horizon if recent price > 30-day average.
- Avoid extrapolating from 18-day history; if 18-day average is > 30-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in short-term trend.
